discovery: Optically addressable single-spin qubits in diamond (NV centers) and their use for quantum sensing and quantum networks
motivation: Wrachtrup and co-workers first optically detected magnetic resonance of a single nitrogen-vacancy spin in diamond, showing that one electron spin in a solid can be initialized, coherently controlled and read out with light at room temperature. Lukin's group turned this fragile quantum property into a tool. They proposed and demonstrated nanoscale NV magnetometry and quantum registers that combine electron and nuclear spins. Hanson achieved spin-photon entanglement between distant NV centers, the loophole-free Bell test (2015) and the first multi-node solid-state quantum network. Together these results created a new field. Solid-state defect spins are now a platform for measurements from single-protein NMR to condensed-matter imaging and neuroscience, and they are a leading architecture for quantum networking. The work has also inspired an entire family of spin-photon interfaces in silicon carbide, silicon and rare-earth hosts. It joins fundamental quantum physics with engineered materials in exceptional ways.
